title: Advanced Transaction Patterns
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of advanced transaction patterns and at least two listed subtopics.

content.intro: Learn advanced transaction patterns through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Advanced Transaction Patterns matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines advanced transaction patterns as part of advanced django architecture. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: transaction.atomic(); Database constraint enforcement; Concurrency and race conditions; Transactional side effects; Safe coordination with external systems. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: transaction.atomic()
items.text: transaction.atomic() affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

items.title: Transactional side effects
items.text: Transactional side effects affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

items.title: Safe coordination with external systems
items.text: Safe coordination with external systems is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to transaction.atomic(). Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
